_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: God stands among us with a plumb line, measuring what we have built.
Set our crooked walls true, O Lord.
A man lay wounded on the Jericho road, and a stranger stopped.
Mercy bent down, poured oil on the wounds, and carried him home.
Give justice to the weak; rescue the lowly and the poor.
This is the worship God asks of us.
Come, and learn to love your neighbor.
Go, and do likewise. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture the road down to Jericho — dust, heat, a man beaten and left in the ditch, and the footsteps of the religious passing by on the far side.
Lord, teach us to do likewise.
Then an outsider, a Samaritan, kneels in the dirt, pours oil and wine into the wounds, lifts him onto his own animal, and pays his way.
Lord, teach us to do likewise.
God holds a plumb line against our lives and asks for justice — defend the weak, lift the fallen, do not look away.
Lord, teach us to do likewise.
So come in from your own long road, be tended and healed, and go back out as neighbor to the next one in the ditch.
Lord, teach us to do likewise. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: God holds a plumb line to all we have built.
Go, and do likewise.
A stranger knelt and poured oil on the wounds.
Go, and do likewise.
Justice for the weak is the worship God wants.
Go, and do likewise.
Come, love your neighbor, and then go.
Go, and do likewise. Amen.
